observation: PR #35 initially described installed skill and subagent assets as generic host capabilities. The first self-shape/consumer run was mechanically green, but exact-diff review showed that the evidence only proved projection: agent-loop could render and install the files. It did not prove host discovery, delegated inheritance, or runtime execution. The model was therefore narrowed to skill-projection and subagent-projection, while bootstrap, delegated bootstrap, pre-tool guardrails, and repository hooks remained separate capability rows. The next multi-source iteration provided a second example of the same evidence discipline: the real pinned voku/agent-skills clean-consumer dogfood passed while the general PHPUnit suite still failed because a CLI output contract changed and a new source-root failure was emitted only on STDERR. No single green evidence surface was sufficient to declare the change complete.

evidence.command: GitHub Actions CI run 31250734064: Agent-loop shapes itself + Installed release-set dogfood + PHP 8.3/8.4/8.5
evidence.summary: The initial typed host matrix and doctor projection passed all CI jobs and clean-consumer dogfood. Manual exact-diff review then found that the names skills/subagents overclaimed what those tests proved, so the capability vocabulary was narrowed to skill-projection/subagent-projection before continuing.

The host model was split by evidence level: skill/subagent projection describes renderer/install mechanics; session bootstrap, subagent bootstrap, pre-tool guardrail, and repository hooks describe separate runtime/lifecycle mechanisms. Unsupported host cells are kept explicit rather than inferred from similarly named vendor features.

evidence.command: GitHub Actions CI run 31251019431: Installed release-set dogfood
evidence.summary: A clean Composer consumer successfully merged agent-loop's package-owned workflow skills with the real voku/agent-skills tree pinned at b5b910666c08e30950e2a5999d9c4a447b31e367 and projected representative engineering skills into Codex, Claude, Copilot, and Antigravity targets.

Despite the real cross-repo consumer passing, composer ci failed two PHPUnit assertions: an existing sync-skills output contract had changed, and a missing explicit skill root was reported only on STDERR while the new behavioral test observed STDOUT. The implementation preserved the old output prefix, appended source-count evidence, and made the operational source-root failure observable consistently.

evidence.command: GitHub Actions CI run 31251220473: tests (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5), Installed release-set dogfood, Agent-loop shapes itself
evidence.summary: After the targeted fixes and documentation alignment, all five jobs passed on head d593e3442cfe0ae1d400961722edae08028bfdc4. The installed consumer again used the real pinned first-party engineering skill source, and the SELF-SHAPE workflow governed the complete PR diff successfully.

The successful self-shape evidence bundle was uploaded with digest sha256:8234cb69236fc6b7dd79cdba9ad964ee60624414693718757a3bf81d548c5a88. The corresponding release-set artifact 9020060670 has digest sha256:e1b98b9f1eb2d83fd7234ea7bdb86cef4c3e07d3087175a0d338a30478c77329.

hypothesis: Agent asset installation is a projection property, not proof that the target coding agent discovers, propagates, or executes the capability. Capability models and completion claims should therefore be no broader than the strongest observed evidence surface, and independent validation surfaces must be allowed to disagree until the discrepancy is resolved.
validated_conclusion: Name and gate coding-agent capabilities at the level actually proven. Treat file rendering/installation as projection evidence; model runtime discovery, delegated propagation, hook lifecycle, and behavioral execution separately. Do not promote a host cell from unsupported/degraded based on a vendor feature name or generated-file presence alone. Likewise, a green specialized dogfood job does not override a failing general contract test: resolve the disagreement before claiming completion.
